entities.summary: Nathaniel Thurmond was an American professional basketball player who spent the majority of his 14-year career in the National Basketball Association (NBA) with the Golden State Warriors franchise. He played the center and power forward positions. Thurmond was a seven-time All-Star and the first player in NBA history to record an official quadruple-double. In 1965, he grabbed 42 rebounds in a game; only Wilt Chamberlain and Bill Russell recorded more rebounds in an NBA game. Thurmond was named a member of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1985, one of the 50 Greatest Players in NBA History, and part of the NBA 75th Anniversary Team in 2021.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a dominant center and power forward in the NBA, Nate Thurmond's impressive statistics, including his quadruple-double achievement and record-breaking 42 rebounds in a single game, had significant regional impact on basketball history. His induction into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1985 solidified his legacy as one of the greatest players in NBA History.
